2. Facts necessary leading to the disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party No.1 as plaintiff instituted other Class Suit Ng 15. of 2005 in the Court of learned ,assistant Judge, Pakundia; Kishoregonj praying for a declaration that the Managing.. Committee constituted with the defendant Nos. 1-10 and 'approved by the defendant No. 12 dated 18.12.03 to be illegal; unlawful; void and not binding upon the plaintiff contending inter-alia that the people of, Shalaudi village of Baruhadia union under police station Pakundia, District. Kishoregonj established a primary school in the year 1985 under the name "Shaluadia Non-Government Primary School". For smooth management of the School, a Managing Committee was formed. That committee appointed the plaintiff as Headmaster of the school and appointed four other teachers. The school started functioning on and from 1.1.1986 and was registered as being "Registered Non-Government, School." on 8.8.1994 and having its registration No. 36. As per circular issued by the Government a Managing Committee was formed with I (eleven) me-ni6ers of which the plaintiffs was the secretary. One man arid one woman" from amongst the persons interested in education and doner were also included as members of the Managing Committee; one of the members of the Managing Committee was from the guardians of the students. Before expiry of the term of Managing Committee, the plaintiff filled up the prescribed for forming a new managing committee. The plaintiff put his signature in the said form and sent the same on .25.9.2002 25.9.2002 to the defendant No. 11 for approval of the same. The list of the new committee was approved-by the defendant No. 13. Thereafter the plaintiff got himself admitted in P. T. 1 institute. Kishoregonj for having a training in the year 2004. He completed his training on 31.12.2004 and joined his post .on 1.1.2.005 as Head Master. During his training period, the defendant No. 10, was functioning as Head Master in 'charge. The plaintiff demanded all 'papers Concerning for that ion of Managing Committee from the defendant No. 10 and the later handed over  papers to the plaintiff but the paper concerning formation  of Managing Committee  was not given to him. 'Subsequently he was supplied the list but that list was not signed by the Upazilla Nirbahi officer. That committee was illegally formed. The defendant No. 10 published the election schedule, on 25.1.05 for formation of the Managing Committee of the school for 2005. The defendant No. 11 and 12 being influenced by the defendant No. 1-10 did not take any steps to give effect of the election schedule. The teachers and other staffs are not getting any salary for which a regular Managing Committee is necessary. The Managing Committee constituted with the defendant No.1-10 and approved on 18:12.03 was an illegal committee. 

 3. After filing the suit the plaintiff made a prayer under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying -for restraining the defendant Nos. 1-10 from performing any as managing committee of the school till disposal of the suit and also restraining them- from raising any hindrance, to the plaintiff in charge of his duties as headmaster. 

 4. That application was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-4 and 610 by filing Written Objection contending, inter alia, that the committee was lawfully framed. The school was registered as Non- Government School on 8.8.1994 having Registration .No. 36. p. e. law a 11 (eleven) members managing committee was framed. The term of the committee was expired on 17.12.2001 Before expiry of the period of said the committee the committee in question was framed as per law: That committee Was duly approved. The plaintiff without getting any prior leave from the Managing 'committee, got himself admitted in PTI Institute, Kishoregonj in the year 1904. The first meeting of the Managing Committee was held 3.9.2004 and the president of the committee duly put signatures upon the paper of the salary for the of July, 2004. Since then the committee has been function in, The plaintiff joined -in the school on 1.1.2005 after completion of the training. Before expiry of the executing committee the plaintiff took an attempt to frame another committee. At this the plaintiff was rebuked by the concerned Upazilla Education Officer. The executing committee held a meeting on 29.1.2005 for taking decision against the .aforementioned activities of the plaintiff and the plaintiff was directed to furnish show cause within 5 (live) days as to why disciplinary action should not be taken against him. It is asserted in the Written Objection that the committee as claimed to have framed by the plaintiff did not function ever and the executing committee constituted by the defendant Nds.1-10 has been functioning. With these averments they prayed for rejection of the temporary injunction prayer. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the said-judgment and order the plaintiff: preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 12.-of 2005 and the said appeal was heard by the learned joint District Judge, 2 Court, Kishoreganj who by the impugned judgment and decree dated. 5.6.2005 allowed the appeal on setting aside the judgment and order of the trial .Court and granted the prayer for temporary injunction. 

 8. Mr. Md. Mozaffar Hossain the learned Advocate for the Petitioner submitted that the plaintiff' being the Headmaster of the school has no locus standi to file a. suit challenging the formation of the managing committee of the school.  He further submitted that the plaintiff. -failed to make out a prima facie and arguable case. Ile further submitted that the committee having started functioning since before the date of filing of the suit, the learned Joint District Judge was not justified in allowing the prayer for temporary injunction. He further submitted that no. case of irreparable loss and injury has been made out by the prayer for temporary injunction is allowed to be continued that will put the whole administration of the school in a position about to deadlock. He prayed for making the rule absolute. 

 9. Mr. Md. Mujibar Rahman, the learned Advocate for the Opposite Party submitted that the learned Joint District. Judge 'on perusal of the material on records allowed the prayer for temporary injunction lawfully. He submitted that a strong and prima facie case in support of prayer for temporary injunction has been made out and the learned. trial Court being failed to consider the said case rejected the prayer for temporary injunction but' the learned Joint District Judge being the appellate Court on perusal  of the prayer for temporary injunction has allowed the said prayer. He submitted that the order impugned in the Rule being a very sound and lawful order there is nothing to interfere with the same: 

 12. The 'defendant Nos. 1-4 '16210:' by submitting Written 'Objection denied the case as made out in the prayer for temporary injunction and at paragraph 13 of the Written Objection they have -categorically stated that the plaintiff himself has accepted the managing committee. in question and has withdrawn his bill under the said Managing committee on making out a clear case with the following terms: 

 These very statements as made in the Written Objection was neither .denied by submitting any counter affidavit nor' any document was produced before the learned Assistant' Judge to show that no payment-of salary was made as per the statements made in the said Written Objection nor the plaintiff denied the fact of receiving salary of July 2004 to December 2004.  13. From the case made-'out in the Written Objection it appears that the Managing committee, in question has started functioning on and from 03.9.2004 and the suit has been filed on 19.2.2005. On perusal of the material on record it is very much clear that no prima facie and arguable case is available to restrain the committee from functioning in view of the fact that the committee has started functioning since its first meeting was held on 3.9.2004 i.e. since long before the filing of the suit. The learned Joint District Judge did not at all consider this, aspect judicially. Admittedly the plaintiff is the Headmaster of the school. Admittedly the committee has accepted his joining after completion of his training. There is no material before us to presume that the plaintiff is being obstructed from functioning, as a headmaster. The learned Joint District Judge has restrained the defendants from dismissing the plaintiff from his post, although no such prayer has been made in the prayer of temporary injunction application. Whether the committee has been framed legally or illegally is a question of fact and that can be decided by the trial Court after taking evidence of both the parties. The Managing Committee in question having started functioning since before the filing of the suit there lies no prayer for temporary injunction against the .said committee as prayed .for. The learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Kishoregonj without considering this very important fact has granted injunction i., illegally. This court at the time of issuing this rule stayed the operation of the impugned order, meaning thereby the committee is still functioning. If the order of injunction sustains that will invite a lot of problems with the smooth administration of the affairs of the school. From the facts and circumstances and discussions made above it is very much clear that the learned. Joint District Judge, 2nd Court Kishoreganj has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in allowing the prayer for temporary injunction. There is merit in the Rule.
